messages:
yasmin: Heads up — noticed a 30-80ms p90 regression on SSE streaming for toolcall routes after today's rollout (merge 9d2f7a1). Affected: hosted API and dedicated canary. :eyes:

kai: saw this in canary too. p50 stable but p90/p99 bumped. Repro with stress-suite on qa.

omar: flamegraphs point to a serialization hotspot inside serialize_tools middleware — lots of small memcpy ops. Also KV prefetch looks like it fires more often.

devon: ran git bisect locally. The regression lands with commit f3c8e2b which changed eventsource framing + added the new "batching_prefetch" heuristic.

perf-bot: CI perf test 'sse_stream_latency' increased 12% on main after merge f3c8e2b (detected 2026-03-18T09:02Z).

kai: profiling notes: kernel autoselect now prefers a tiled transpose kernel for certain seq-len patterns. That kernel has an extra copy step when KV prefetch is enabled. Combined cost ~= 20-40ms for long chats.

yasmin: can we pin down whether it's framing change OR prefetch heuristic OR serialization change? We need to decide on a rollback vs targeted revert. Holding rollout for now.

devon: quick repro command I used: `stress-client --suite sse-toolcall --concurrency 120 --seq-dist=short-long` — attach profile: http://perf.internal/flame/2150007777 (private).

omar: experiment: disabled prefetch in runtime config and reran. p95 dropped back ~35ms. So prefetch threshold bump looks causal. Config diff: ``
runtime.yaml: 
  batching_prefetch: 
    enabled: true
    threshold: 64  # changed from 16 in f3c8e2b
``

kai: interesting — why would raising threshold increase latency? Our prefetch path currently schedules a prefetched KV copy that runs inline for first response; if it misroutes kernels we pay a transpose penalty.

yasmin: ok plan: (1) revert the threshold change in canary to 16 (2) add a quick patch to move prefetch to background thread (async) in serialize_tools, (3) run canary perf suite.

build-bot: Revert PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4983 — reverting f3c8e2b. CI: running perf/regressions.

devon: bisect logs: `git bisect start; git bisect bad main~0; git bisect good main~5;` -> f3c8e2b. Confirmed.

omar: also noticed the EventSource framing change added an extra header encode step for tool-call metadata. That adds ~5-8ms per handshake when combined with prefetch work.

kai: low-risk quickfix: change prefetch threshold back and gate prefetch with `if (!streaming_toolcall)` — we only need aggressive prefetch for non-streaming batch routes.

yasmin: agree. I'll push a canary revert for the threshold and hold the rollout. If perf looks good after canary, we can merge a more robust async prefetch design.

perf-bot: Canary perf run finished: sse_stream_latency p95 reduced by 28ms after threshold revert. No other regressions.

yasmin: awesome. Reverting rollout hold and continue with rollback/patch plan. Thanks all — follow-up doc in #eng-runtime about async prefetch design and kernel autoselect safety checks. :thumbsup:
